title: SELECT and result columns
text: A SELECT query reads data and returns rows. The expressions after SELECT determine the columns or calculated values in each returned row. FROM determines the input tables or subqueries. Explain only the columns and expressions that are actually present.

title: WHERE filters rows
text: WHERE filters the input rows before later grouping and result calculation. An explanation should state the actual predicate and its effect without inventing extra filters. Do not claim a row is included when the predicate is false or NULL.

title: JOIN combines input datasets
text: A JOIN combines rows from two input sources according to its join type and constraint. Explain the actual tables, aliases, join condition, and join type present in the SQL. Never invent a relationship that is not written or supported by the schema.

title: GROUP BY and aggregate functions
text: GROUP BY forms groups from the filtered input. Aggregate functions such as COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX calculate values over rows or groups. Explain the grouping columns and actual aggregate expressions that occur in the query.

title: HAVING filters groups
text: HAVING is evaluated for groups after grouping. It should not be described as an ordinary row-level WHERE filter. Mention the actual HAVING condition and what groups it removes.

title: ORDER BY and LIMIT
text: ORDER BY controls the order of returned rows. ASC sorts upward and DESC downward when specified. LIMIT restricts how many rows are returned and OFFSET skips an initial number of rows. Only mention these behaviors when the SQL contains them.

title: Subqueries and CTEs
text: A subquery is a SELECT nested inside another query. A CTE introduced with WITH gives a named query result that can be referenced by the outer query. Explain nested logic only when it is present, and keep the outer and inner conditions distinct.

title: UNION INTERSECT EXCEPT
text: Compound SELECT operators combine the results of multiple SELECT statements. UNION removes duplicate rows while UNION ALL keeps them; INTERSECT keeps common rows; EXCEPT keeps rows from the left query that are absent from the right query. State the operator actually used.

title: Window functions
text: A window function computes a value across a related set of rows while retaining a result for each input row. PARTITION BY divides rows into partitions and an ORDER BY inside OVER controls the window ordering. Do not confuse a window function with GROUP BY, which reduces rows into groups.

title: NULL and SQL three-valued logic
text: NULL has special comparison behavior in SQL. A WHERE predicate that evaluates to NULL does not pass the row. IS NULL and IS NOT NULL explicitly test for NULL. Do not replace NULL semantics with ordinary equality or inequality in an explanation.

title: Ground explanations in the query
text: The SQL and supplied schema are the authoritative evidence. Generic SQL knowledge can clarify syntax, but it cannot justify invented columns, tables, data values, business rules, joins, filters, or intentions. If the query does not contain an operation, do not require it in the explanation.

title: Write concise SQL explanations
text: A strong explanation says what data is read, which rows are filtered, how rows are combined or grouped when applicable, what values are calculated, and how results are ordered or limited when those operations exist. Prefer concrete references to the actual query over vague SQL definitions.
